question.problem: Use trial and error to find the solutions, if any, to the congruence $4x≡5\,(\text{mod}\,8).$

current_example.problem: Use trial and error to find the solutions, if any, to the congruence $2x \equiv 4 \:(\text{mod}\:6).$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=6$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x = 0,1,2,3,4,5$ into the equation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot 0 & ≡0≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 1 & ≡2≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 2 & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & ✓ \\ 2\cdot 3 & ≡0≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 4 & ≡2≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 5 & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x\equiv 2, 5$ only $(\textrm{mod}\:6).$
